# Pipes Pipes are used to move gases from one place to another. Many types of pipe are available for construction:
Pipes [color=#a4885c]automatically connect[/color] to other pipes when secured to the hull with a wrench, forming a [textlink="pipe network" link="PipeNetworks"]. A pipe network is commonly called a [textlink="pipenet" link="PipeNetworks"].
Pipes [color=red]do not connect[/color] to pipes that are already connected to another pipe. For example, you cannot place a bent pipe over a straight pipe to create an improvised T-junction.
However, two pipes can occupy the same tile as long as neither blocks the other pipe's connection. For example, two bent pipes can share one tile: one can carry gas from north to east while the other carries it from west to south.
Pipes and most gas-handling equipment can be painted with a spray painter. This is commonly done to distinguish the air and waste sections of the station's distribution pipenet.
